facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: In April of 1990, I was sitting in my office at Giza when a guard came to tell me that an American tourist had been thrown from her horse when the animal stumbled over the remains of a mud-brick wall.
facts.text: In 1990, Egyptian archaeologists led by Zahi Hawass discovered the Cemetery of the Pyramid Builders after an American tourist's horse tripped over a buried mudbrick wall at Giza.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Among these is the beautifully decorated tomb of the overseer of linen, the overseer of the royal house of purification, Nefertheith.
facts.source_name: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Egypt
facts.text: Inscriptions on the tombs of the builders at Giza revealed proud official titles including overseer of linen, royal purifier, master craftsmen, and directors of the pyramid side.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: graffiti was found above the king's chamber in the Great Pyramid that, among other names, included 'Friends of Khufu Gang.'
facts.text: Quarry marks painted in red ochre inside the relieving chambers of the Great Pyramid preserve the names of proud work gangs, such as the Friends of Khufu Gang.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: We have examined and identified over 175,000 bones and bone fragments from the excavations at the Giza pyramid settlement... prime beef for pyramid builders.
facts.text: Archaeozoologist Richard Redding identified over 175,000 animal bone fragments at the Giza settlement, calculating that the workforce received more than 1,800 kilograms of meat daily from cattle, sheep, and goats.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The majority of the bodies discovered show evidence of hard physical labor, many even featuring broken bones. Most of these had healed correctly, however, indicating that, in addition to being well-fed, the workers also received very good medical care.
facts.source_name: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Egypt
facts.text: Skeletal remains from the workers' cemetery showed evidence of skilled medical interventions, including professionally set bone fractures and trepanations that completely healed before death.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: In 2013 archaeologists uncovered what has since been called 'the greatest discovery in Egypt in the 21st century': hundreds of papyrus fragments dating to the last years of King Khufu's reign at the oldest harbour in Egypt, a site on the Red Sea coast called Wadi al-Jarf.
facts.text: In 2013, archaeologists directed by Pierre Tallet unearthed the Diary of Merer at Wadi al-Jarf, the world's oldest written papyrus detailing how an elite boat crew transported limestone blocks for the Great Pyramid.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: archaeological evidence points to a beef-rich diet for the overseers, while the general workers ate much more sheep and goat meat, in addition to the grain and beer consumed by most citizens.
facts.text: Specialists debate whether high-quality cattle meat was shared widely among all rotating stone haulers or reserved primarily for administrative supervisors and permanent artisans.

Setting: dramatic view of the Great Pyramid of Giza under a towering desert dust storm at sunset, orange sky, sand whipping across the plateau, a row of small mudbrick tombs half buried in the foreground, natural light, documentary photograph. Correction after review: Remove the centre watermark or make it much fainter; the corner SG logo is enough. Time of day and light, overriding anything darker in the setting above: bright golden-hour sunlight or clear daylight, a blue or golden sky, warm saturated colours, his face and clothes fully lit; never night, dusk, storm clouds, lightning, fog, grey overcast, a dark or desaturated look. The background is real and in motion behind him (as fits the place: waves, mist, leaves, flags, lamps flickering, people walking, traffic, light shifting); never a still, flat or heavily blurred backdrop. If the scene shows the past of an Indian story, it is ancient India (a story from another country keeps that country's own dress and buildings): Indian people in dhotis, sarees and angavastram, warriors with bows, spears and bronze or leather armour, carved stone pillars, oil lamps; never European knights, plate armour, castles or anything medieval European. Movement and framing: like a TV news reporter on location, he walks toward the camera while he speaks: he starts three or four steps back, seen from the knees up, walks steadily and confidently toward the lens, and stops at a medium shot from the waist up for the last words. His whole head and both shoulders stay inside the frame the whole time, with clear space above his hair and on both sides; do not crop the top of his head. Lighting: warm key light on the face, a soft rim light on the hair, matched to the scene; flattering, no harsh shadows, no dull or flat grey look. SG [locked] walking tall and lively, shoulders open, energetic and confident, wearing a maroon kurta with a gold-bordered stole. Speaks from the first frame, mouth matched to the words, steady eye contact with the lens. Face and delivery: an excited, high-energy presenter breaking a big story, full of life, as if he cannot wait to tell you. Bright, wide-awake eyes, lively eyebrows that lift on the question, a big, bright, genuine smile. On the question his voice rises with excitement as he strides closer. On the last line a big confident smile, a quick nod and a point at the viewer. Natural blinking, lively head movement. Never sad, gloomy, worried, tired, sleepy, flat or bored; never a frown, never a blank face. Voice: energetic, upbeat, punchy and clear, a brisk pace, rising on the question, with a quick beat before the last line. Hands: energetic, natural gestures at chest height: a quick point toward the scene behind him on the question and an open palm toward the viewer on the last line; never limp, never hanging still by his sides. Camera: eye level, steady, holding its place as he walks up to it (a very slight slow push-in at most), slight handheld feel.
